name: Cloud with Rain
tldr: 🌧️ usually reports rain, while also adding gloom, misery, or tears to a casual message.

contextMeanings.meaning: It refers to rain, wet weather, or a forecast that may affect plans.
It exaggerates a disappointing, tiring, or miserable situation as dreary weather.
contextMeanings.example: this week decided to be awful 🌧️

contextMeanings.meaning: It jokingly claims that conditions are terrible when the situation is merely inconvenient or exaggerated.
It flags rain as a practical issue that could delay travel, an outdoor event, or site work.
contextMeanings.example: storms may delay the site visit 🌧️

platformNotes.note: In family and friend threads, it often appears after a forecast or a change of plans. Because the image is visually literal, it can be read as a quick weather update before the sentence’s emotional tone.
In captions and comment replies, it can make a comment about a miserable day more expressive. It also appears on outfit, travel, and weather-related posts when rain is part of the picture.
On TikTok, comments often use it as shorthand for a bleak or annoying moment. A video showing real rain may use it plainly, so the clip usually supplies the needed context.
In Slack, the clearest use is attached to logistics, such as saying rain may affect travel. A bare emoji can sound unserious when a team needs an unmistakable schedule update.

generationalNotes.note: Many younger users treat 🌧️ as casual shorthand for a mood, a bad day, or exaggerated sadness rather than as a literal forecast.
Millennials commonly recognize both uses, reading 🌧️ as rain when weather is being discussed and as atmospheric gloom when it follows a complaint.
Gen X users may lean more heavily toward the literal weather meaning, especially when the emoji appears without playful or emotional language.

warnings.title: Mistaking weather for emotional distress
warnings.description: A sender may simply be reporting rain while the recipient assumes they need comfort or consolation. Mention the weather plainly when practical information matters.

seoDescription: What does 🌧️ mean? It usually reports rainy weather, but it can also underline a gloomy mood, miserable plans, or tears in casual messages.

longForm.overview:
🌧️ is often mistaken for a dramatic cry, a plea for comfort, or evidence that the sender is upset. Those readings can be right, but the emoji is also one of the plainest ways to mention actual rain. A friend sending “it’s pouring 🌧️” may simply be telling you to bring an umbrella, not asking you to emotionally support them. The context and surrounding words decide whether it is weather talk or a mood marker.

Unlike ☁️, which shows a cloud without precipitation, 🌧️ includes visible rain. It therefore leans more strongly toward wet, gloomy, or unpleasant conditions than a general “cloudy” emoji. Compared with 🌦️, which pairs sun and rain in one image, 🌧️ presents the weather as steadily rainy rather than changeable. Still, people often use it figuratively to underline a bad day or a burst of tears without spelling out either one. The apparent sadness is part of its look, but it is not automatically a confession.
longForm.howPeopleUseIt:
🌧️ shows up most often when weather changes the conversation: a friend asks whether to walk, someone mentions a soaked commute, or people make plans. In those cases the emoji saves the sender from writing a forecast; the surrounding sentence tells you whether the practical point is the rain or the annoyance it causes.

It also appears when people want to underline a mood without choosing a face. “this week is relentless 🌧️” is more atmospheric than a plain description of a difficult week. Sometimes the tears are teasing, as in “you made me cry 🌧️,” but the emoji does not establish that reading on its own. People may also use it to make a bad moment look theatrically gloomy.
longForm.whenNotToUse:
Avoid 🌧️ when the message needs precise, practical information. Saying “road conditions may be dangerous 🌧️” is less helpful than naming the danger, the expected timing, and what people should do. The same applies to work updates: if rain could affect attendance or a deadline, state that clearly instead of relying on the image alone.

It can also seem tonally wrong after someone shares grief, illness, or painful news. A rain cloud may look like you are adding gloom to an already heavy moment. Do not use it to minimize someone’s feelings or as an automatic substitute for a crying emoji. If the point is sadness, use 😭 or 😢; if it is weather, keep the message factual.
longForm.howToReply:
If someone sends 🌧️, first check whether they are reporting weather or describing the mood. For practical rain, match it with ☔ or say “take an umbrella.” For a bad mood, acknowledge the situation with “rough week” or respond with 😭 when that feels natural. Asking “is it actually raining or are you being dramatic?” can playfully resolve the ambiguity.

If the emoji appears on your own message or post, receiving 🌧️ usually means the scene looked bleak, disappointing, or very wet. You can lean into that with a caption such as “the sky won today.” Do not assume it is criticism of you. If you need people to take a weather-related warning seriously, follow the emoji with clear details rather than repeating more weather symbols.

faqs.question: What does 🌧️ mean from a guy?
faqs.answer: It may literally mean it is raining. If there is no weather context, he could be using it to describe a gloomy mood or a situation he finds miserable; it does not by itself signal romantic interest.

faqs.question: Is 🌧️ flirty?
faqs.answer: Not on its own. It can appear in a flirty conversation, but the words around it—not the rain cloud—will usually reveal whether he is talking about weather, sadness, or teasing you.

faqs.question: What does 🌧️ mean on TikTok?
faqs.answer: In comments and captions, it often means the video or situation feels depressing, annoying, or hopeless. When the clip shows obvious rain, it may simply be naming the weather.

faqs.question: What is the difference between 🌧️ and 🌦️?
faqs.answer: 🌧️ shows a cloud with falling rain and suggests steady wet weather. 🌦️ shows sun with rain, so it points more toward changeable conditions with brighter spells.

conversationExamples.message: can’t make it tonight, it’s pouring 🌧️ want to reschedule?
conversationExamples.interpretation: This is most likely a practical weather cancellation, not a coded romantic rejection. Reply warmly and agree on another time if you are still interested.

conversationExamples.message: my plans are completely falling apart 🌧️
conversationExamples.interpretation: The sender is dramatizing how disappointing the day feels. Offer sympathy or a joke, depending on your relationship, rather than assuming they need serious help.

conversationExamples.message: rain is hammering the office and the roads are already flooded 🌧️
conversationExamples.interpretation: The emoji emphasizes the severity of the weather and may support a request for flexibility. Respond with concrete travel or schedule information.

conversationExamples.message: brought completely the wrong shoes for this weather 🌧️
conversationExamples.interpretation: This is a light complaint about being caught in the rain. A teasing reply about bad planning fits better than emotional reassurance.

conversationExamples.message: caption me looking defeated under this sky 🌧️
conversationExamples.interpretation: The sender wants the rain to make the picture feel moody and cinematic. Match the joke with a dramatic caption or another gloomy weather image.
